tasks.short: Encourage patients and attend to delegated physical needs under therapist supervision.

steps.what: Retrieve the therapist's current delegated instructions and relevant patient precautions
Listen to the patient and observe immediate physical needs
Encourage patients during the delegated activity
Attend to physical needs within the therapist's delegated instructions
Check and communicate immediate concerns to the supervising therapist

tasks.design: Configure a patient-linked instruction view in {OTHER}, the clinical records system. The aide retrieves existing delegated instructions, then provides personal encouragement and physical assistance; immediate concern communication remains a separate human action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current delegated instructions can require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: A native patient-linked view may shorten that lookup without changing the care activity.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding the patient's needs and staying within delegated competence.
tasks.altitude: Protect patient-facing time while making current instructions easier to find.

evidence.claim: A native patient-linked instruction view may reduce navigation while hands-on assistance remains human; benefit is E1.

assumptions: Patient encouragement and physical assistance are counted here. The actual observation record is fully represented in task 9400, and the routine progress report in 9399; immediate concern communication is distinct from that routine report.

The supervising therapist supplies patient identity, instruction version and precautions through the existing delegated-work contract. The aide checks them in s1; therapist preparation is existing work, not new unpaid labour. Missing or unclear instructions require manual clarification with lookup effort retained.
The native clinical view is tested first. No model selects care or generates physical instructions.
No hidden note writing sits in s2-s5; record entry is explicitly owned by task 9400.
unknowns: Whether the clinical system already shows delegated instructions directly
Actual lookup effort and access permissions
research_questions: Does a patient-linked view remove navigation without increasing instruction ambiguity or supervisor workload?

already_counted.description: Human retrieval and matching of current instructions

incremental.description: Maintain the instruction view and access mapping

approvals.approved_version: The exact observed concern, patient identity and supervising therapist checked immediately before communication; new observations require a fresh check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R98 gives2 gross minus1 upkeep =1 net. Low: instruction versions are poorly linked and lookup still takes9 of its10 baseline hours, R99; net0. High: the native view identifies the current instruction but manual patient matching remains, lookup8.5 plus90 unchanged gives R98.5; net0.5 after1 upkeep. All patient interaction and physical assistance remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and communicate factual patient progress reports to the supervising therapist.

steps.what: Retrieve the patient's recorded attendance, progress, attitudes and accomplishments
Select relevant factual observations and distinguish uncertainty from observed progress
Write the patient progress report or speaking notes from the selected observations

loop.purpose: Draft a factual report from aide-selected observations
loop.input: Selected source observations, reporting period and supervisor's request
loop.output: Draft factual summary with source links and uncertainties
loop.check: Aide checks every statement against the record and removes inferred attitudes, diagnoses or unobserved progress
loop.stop: One revision; conflicting sources or unsupported statements return the report to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A report template supplies fields but cannot condense varied factual observations

steps.what: Check the report's patient, period and factual content against the sources
Check the final report and communicate it to the supervisor or therapist

tasks.design: Use a native period view in {OTHER}, the clinical records system, and a bounded factual draft in {DOCS}. Selecting observations, writing the report, checking it and delivering the final report to the supervising colleague are separate actions; the draft makes no treatment recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source navigation and phrasing factual reports add effort.
tasks.enabler_now: A source-linked drafting step can condense aide-selected observations for human checking.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing observations from interpretation and reporting uncertainty honestly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowledge of the actual encounter and accountability to the supervising clinician.
tasks.altitude: Prepare concise factual handovers with less repeated wording.

reach.task: Trace the source of a reported observation

evidence.claim: Fysio.AI drafts a structured physiotherapy intake and asks the therapist to check it; this is an adjacent drafting capability, not a validated aide progress-report result.
The proposed report preparation benefit is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: Task 9400 owns initial observation capture and maintenance of the client record. This task owns a requested report assembled from that existing record, including written preparation and actual communication.

The aide selects patient identity and reporting period in s1 and supplies selected source observations in s2. Capture and selection effort remain counted; absent records or conflicting facts require manual reporting.
Native report views and templates are tested before the drafting loop. No unattended report send or clinical decision is proposed.
Ordinary author saves during drafting and correction stay fully retained without approval; the gate is on communicating the exact final report.
unknowns: Approved environment for drafting health information
research_questions: Does reviewed factual drafting save report preparation time after checking every observation and uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Report draft review and full factual checking

incremental.description: Maintain report prompts and sample factual fidelity

approvals.approved_version: Exact final factual report, patient identity, reporting period and supervising recipient checked before communication; any revision requires a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R82 gives18 gross minus3 upkeep =15 net. Low: source observations lack timestamps and most narrative needs rewriting, leaving retrieval19, writing32 plus45 unchanged, R96; net1. High: period metadata are usable but interpretation-sensitive wording needs editing, leaving17+26+45=88 retained; net9 after3 upkeep. Selection, factual checking and actual handover remain full.

tasks.short: Observe patient activity and separately write, check and maintain the client record.

steps.what: Retrieve the correct client record and delegated observation requirements
Observe patients' attendance, progress, attitudes and accomplishments during the delegated activity
Record the patient observations and attendance in the client record
Check recorded information for patient matching, factual accuracy and delegated scope
Maintain encounter identifiers and supporting record links for later retrieval

tasks.design: Configure encounter-linked observation forms and record views in {OTHER}, the clinical records system. Observation, factual entry, checking and maintaining record links are separately timed; no inference of patient attitudes or autonomous clinical note is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated record navigation, encounter fields and observation headings add entry effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms and encounter defaults can reduce repeated metadata handling.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate factual observation and distinguishing an observation from a clinical conclusion.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what was actually observed and when the supervising clinician must clarify scope.
tasks.altitude: Maintain clearer factual records with less repeated entry.

evidence.claim: Native encounter forms and reusable observation headings may reduce entry handling; benefit is E1.
The digest describes Dutch dossier responsibility under the therapist; the proposed aide form does not transfer that responsibility.

assumptions: This task owns the actual client observation record, including capture, checking and maintenance; a separate requested progress report belongs to task 9399.

The aide identifies patient and encounter in s1, observes attendance and factual activity in s2 and captures encounter date, author, observation text and attendance status in s3. Missing identifiers require manual matching with time retained.
Native forms are tested before custom software. No ambient recording, inferred emotion or automatic clinical interpretation is proposed.
Existing supervisor responsibility continues without added review labour being claimed as free. The aide's ordinary internal saves stay fully retained and require no invented approval stage.
unknowns: Permitted aide record fields and existing supervisor workflow
Existing encounter defaults and duplicate entry
research_questions: Can native encounter defaults reduce repeated metadata entry while keeping factual text and checks intact?

already_counted.description: Factual observation and record accuracy checks

incremental.description: Maintain observation forms and encounter mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R88.5 gives11.5 gross minus2 upkeep =9.5 net. Low: encounter identifiers are incomplete and most fields cannot default, leaving retrieval9, entry29 and maintenance9 plus50 unchanged, R97; net1. High: encounter metadata are compatible but observation text remains personal, leaving9+25+8+50=92 retained; net6 after2 upkeep. No saving comes from a same-system save.

tasks.short: Prepare the treatment area and equipment, count supplies and separately maintain inventory records.

steps.what: Retrieve the delegated work area, equipment and supply preparation requirements
Prepare and maintain the work area and treatment materials
Check and maintain the delegated treatment equipment
outputs: checked and maintained equipment or identified concern

steps.what: Count treatment and educational supplies and identify stock discrepancies
Maintain the inventory record with observed counts and equipment preparation exceptions
inputs: checked and maintained equipment or identified concern
outputs: updated supply inventory and preparation record

tasks.design: Link preparation instructions in {DOCS} and configure a supply-entry view in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Physical preparation, equipment work and counting remain fully human; inventory and exception writing are separate from those physical actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated supply identifiers and stock record layout add clerical effort after counting.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item lists and count forms can reduce repeated entry without changing physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Correct preparation and recognising equipment or supply discrepancies.
tasks.human_edge: Direct inspection of the physical treatment environment.
tasks.altitude: Keep an accessible inventory with less repeated record handling.

reach.task: Maintain a clear preparation exception record
reach.learn: Item identity and concise factual entries

evidence.claim: Native item lists and count-entry forms can support supply records; benefit for this task is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The baseline includes inventory record entry separately from physical supply counting and equipment preparation. No new procurement or ordering workflow is added.

The aide produces item identity, location, count and discrepancy observation in s4 and captures them in s5; equipment exceptions come from s3. Capture effort is counted. Unidentified items and uncertain counts are resolved manually.
Native stock forms and instruction links precede custom software. No assumed par-level input, automated reorder or alert is proposed.
The author's ordinary internal save stays fully retained without self-approval or separate saving.
unknowns: Existing inventory system and item identifiers
Actual record entry effort and equipment exception frequency
research_questions: Can a native item list reduce count transcription while leaving every physical count and inspection intact?

already_counted.description: Physical preparation, equipment work and counting

incremental.description: Maintain supply identifiers and entry layout

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R93 gives7 gross minus1 upkeep =6 net. Low: supply labels do not match the record and preparation exceptions need bespoke text, leaving lookup5 and entry19 plus75 physical work, R99; net0. High: common item identifiers fit the native form but count and exception checks remain, leaving lookup4 and entry17 plus75, R96; net3 after1 upkeep. Physical work is fully retained.

role.altitude: Keep delegated patient support personal while making factual records and supplies easier to maintain.
reach: Help therapy colleagues trace factual observation sources
Support clear supply and preparation records
role.ambitious_version: An aide with clearer records and protected time for supervised hands-on patient support.
